name: children-forwarding
body:
`children` is a layout constructor that forwards a caller's authored `.data.<section>` entries as child sections of a `section` helper call: `(children "<name>" .data.<section>)`. Its first argument names the section template to instantiate, and its second is the caller's `.data` list for a declared section; each entry in that list is re-instantiated as a child of the helper target with that template — its fields are the entry's source field values, its body the entry's source body, and its own children the entry's own `.data` — so a layout passes on the authored section instances it received without re-listing them. The forwarded children resolve exactly as literal `child` arguments do: the target's declared `sections:` accept the template, the declaration's min/max are counted over the forwarded set, the child template's fields and body validate, each child's own sub-children come from the entry's `.data`, and each child gets its own `.item` descriptor (child-constructor, section-data-context). A `children` value is consumed only as a child argument of a `section` call; because a `.data` list is a runtime value, a `children` call is not inspected at load and is checked against the target's declared sections when the target renders (section-helper-load-checks). `children` reads only the `.data` list passed to it and adds no data access of its own.

AC: `{{ section "columns" nil nil (children "column" .data.columns) }}` re-instantiates the caller's authored `column` entries as the target's children, each keeping its source fields and body; an entry with its own children forwards them; a forwarded set that leaves a declared section below its min is a render-time error naming the declaration; `children` used outside a `section` call's child-argument position is a layout value, not a rendered section.
